research_question: How should commit-bound evidence distinguish a workflow run that was not expected from an expected run that is absent, without treating incomplete enumeration as proof?

sources.title: GitHub Actions workflow syntax
supports: Multiple configured events independently trigger workflows.
Push and pull request path filters restrict execution to matching changed paths.
workflow_dispatch is a distinct manual trigger.

sources.title: GitHub REST API endpoints for workflow runs
supports: Workflow-run observations are API results whose completeness depends on endpoint, filters, and pagination.
The retained-evidence workflow configures workflow_dispatch, push, and pull_request.
Push and pull_request use seven exact path filters.

sources.observation: The available connector returned zero workflow runs.

finding: Trigger expectation and run observation are separate evidence layers. A zero-result observation is only expected_run_absent when path/event expectation is proven and workflow-run enumeration is independently complete. Otherwise the result must remain expectation_unproven or observation_unproven.
uncertainty: No exhaustive authenticated workflow-run enumeration was available in this run.
No live workflow dispatch was performed.
The path contract is intentionally exact to the current retained-evidence workflow and must be updated when that workflow changes.
falsification_route: Provide complete changed-path evidence for a commit and show that the classifier disagrees with GitHub's documented trigger semantics.
Provide exhaustive all-event workflow-run enumeration proving a run exists where the classifier says run_not_expected, or proving no run exists where it says run_expected.
Modify the workflow path filters without updating the contract and demonstrate stale classification.
